hypotheses.justification: The conclusion is the Gaussian Poincaré inequality, independent of a Clark–Ocone family. The checked definitions make mderiv the covariance Cameron–Martin gradient and mderivD12 its graph closure. A direct proof starts with smooth bounded f and the Gaussian Ornstein–Uhlenbeck averaging operators Q_t, centered at the mean of P. Gaussian integration by parts gives Var_P(f) = 2∫₀∞ ‖D Q_t f‖₂² dt; the gradient identity D Q_t f = exp(-t) Q_t(Df) and Jensen give Var_P(f) ≤ 2∫₀∞ exp(-2t)‖Df‖₂² dt = ‖Df‖₂². These identities follow first in finite-dimensional Gaussian coordinates and then by conditional Gaussian approximation, without requiring invertible covariance. Finally, inGraphClosure_mderivClosure supplies smooth bounded approximants converging together with their derivatives; passing to their L² limits proves the stated inequality. The checked expectationL2 definition is precisely the constant expectation. IsGaussian already makes P a probability measure, excluding the zero measure; for a Dirac Gaussian, including trivial W, the centered left side is zero. Thus no Brownian process, filtration property, or data from C is required.
